subject: maths
question: A man covers two-third of a certain distance at the speed of 70 km/h and the rest at the speed of 50 km/h. It takes him {6(4)/(5)} hours for the whole journey. At a speed of 56 km/h, in what time will he be able to cover the entire distance?
solution:
**Given:**

Total time = 6(4)/(5) = (34)/(5) hrs

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance/Speed

**Calculation:**

Let the distance between the two points be '3X'

The person travels 2X distance with a speed of 70 km/h

He travels the remaining X distance with a speed of 50 km/h

Using the formula, for the whole journey

34/5 = 2X/70 + X/50

⇒ 34/5 = 17X/350

⇒ X = 2 × 70 = 140 km

∴ Distance (3X) = 140 × 3 = 420km

Time taken to travel this distance with a speed of 56 km/h,

Time = 420/56 = 15/2

Or Time = 7(1)/(2) hrs.

**∴ Time taken to travel the complete distance will be 7(1)/(2) hrs.**
